extracted.intended_audience: University of Pennsylvania investigators and research staff preparing grant proposals (especially NIH applicants) and research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Penn researchers on preparing competitive grant proposals (NIH-centric but covering NSF/DOE/foundations), with Penn-specific resource citation and ORS pre-submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims — standard four-paragraph structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims page conventions: Standard four-paragraph structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the conventional four-paragraph layout for the Specific Aims page; be concise and iterative. Include a clear hypothesis and succinctly state aims. A conceptual figure is encouraged. Iterate the page many times (recommendation: 10+ iterations) to refine clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis-driven aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Aims should be hypothesis-driven rather than purely descriptive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame aims around testable hypotheses; reviewers prefer hypothesis-driven proposals over descriptive studies. Tie hypotheses to mechanistic questions and translational endpoints where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Each aim should be independent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design aims so that the success/failure of one aim does not invalidate the others. Independent aims strengthen reviewability and reduce risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual figure encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a conceptual figure on the Specific Aims page where helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single clear schematic can help non-specialist reviewers grasp the overall plan and hypothesis quickly; use to show relationships among aims/mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterate Specific Aims extensively
rubrics_metrics.description: Iterate the Specific Aims page many times (recommendation: 10+ iterations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polish wording, flow, and clarity through repeated revision; solicit internal feedback to ensure it reads well to non-specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame significance for non-specialist reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance should be framed so non-specialist reviewers understand importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the problem and impact in terms accessible to reviewers outside your immediate subfield; connect to broader health/ scientific priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite high-impact recent papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use recent high-impact literature in the Significance section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate awareness of up-to-date major advances and place your work in that context; cite landmark and recent high-impact studies to justify importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connect to NIH institute mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Link proposal aims to the mission/priorities of the target NIH institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly explain how the project aligns with the funding institute’s goals and priorities to improve reviewer alignment and responsiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame innovation as a novel application
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe innovation as a novel application or approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize what is new about your approach or application of methods; be realistic about feasibility while highlighting novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach — organize each aim with subsections
rubrics_metrics.description: In Approach, present each aim broken into clear subsections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each aim include rationale, methods, expected outcomes, potential pitfalls and alternatives; use headings/subsections to improve readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis plan required
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a clear statistical analysis plan in the Approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe statistical tests, models, and analysis workflows that will be used for each aim; make clear how analyses will test hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power calculation and sample size justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide power calculations and justify sample sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how the proposed sample size achieves desired power for primary outcomes; justify assumptions and effect sizes used in calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor and reproducibility language
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly address rigor and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include statements about experimental design, blinding/randomization where applicable, replication, data handling, and steps taken to ensure reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication (materials and methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide authentication details for biological/technical materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe authentication of cell lines, reagents, antibodies, and other key materials as part of rigor and reproducibility commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address sex as a biological variable
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for sex as a biological variable where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe plans for inclusion/analysis by sex or rationale for single-sex studies; follow NIH SABV expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss alternatives / contingency plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Include alternative approaches and contingency plans for likely pitfalls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate major risks and present feasible alternative strategies to demonstrate the project’s resilience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator productivity proportionate to career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate investigator productivity appropriate for their career stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor CV and biosketch emphasis to show an appropriate track record; early-career investigators should highlight productivity and trajectory, senior investigators should show sustained outputs and leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence narrative for Early Stage Investigator (ESI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear narrative of independence for ESIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how the PI is independent from prior mentors (unique resources, distinct aims, separate funding streams) and justify eligibility when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite Penn-specific resources in Investigator/Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite Penn cores, centers, and institutional resources (e.g., CHOP, Wistar, ITMAT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly reference relevant Penn cores/facilities and institutional strengths to strengthen Environment and feasibility arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of support should be specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain letters of support that are specific to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should detail concrete commitments, resources, and how collaborators/cores will contribute; generic letters are less persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite appropriate Penn cores and facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage and cite Penn cores and facilities (e.g., Single Cell Biology, Genomics Core, Genome Frontiers Institute, Cancer Center cores).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the exact core and describe the services to be used; mentioning named Penn cores strengthens feasibility and institutional support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite relevant Penn training programs where applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference Penn training programs (MSTP, Biomedical Graduate Studies, Engineering PhD programs, ITMAT training) when relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use training programs to support education/training plans, career development, and institutional environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to ORS pre-submission timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow ORS timeline: 6 weeks for budget/admin docs, 2–4 weeks for full draft review, 1 week for final compliance check; ORS submits 5 days before deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan internal deadlines to meet ORS milestones; allow time for budget reconciliation, mock review, and final compliance checks to avoid last-minute issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use department-level mock reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject proposals to department-level mock reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct internal mock peer review to surface scientific, methodological, and clarity issues before cross-department or ORS review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-department review for interdisciplinary work
rubrics_metrics.description: Use cross-department review for interdisciplinary proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicit feedback from multiple departments/units to ensure clarity and rigor across disciplinary boundaries and to catch integration problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORS formatting and compliance check
rubrics_metrics.description: ORS performs a formatting and compliance check prior to submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect ORS to verify format, institutional compliance, sponsor requirements, and administrative completeness; address flagged items promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic budget with Penn indirect rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a realistic budget using Penn’s negotiated indirect (F&A) rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure budgets reflect true costs and Penn’s indirect rate; unrealistic budgets or incorrect rates are common grounds for issues during ORS review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance must be addressed (IRB/IACUC/etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address all compliance requirements (IRB, IACUC, human subjects protections, CHOP IRB where relevant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document approvals or clear plans to obtain them; for CHOP/Penn collaborative projects, determine which institution’s IRB is applicable early to avoid submission gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penn-CHOP-Wistar subaward coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate and manage subaward complexities for Penn-CHOP-Wistar collaborations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify subaward roles, budgets, compliance responsibilities and timelines early; ORS will flag subaward complications pre-submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid common pre-submission errors (budget, format, missing sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORS commonly catches budget errors, format violations, missing required sections, and compliance gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run a complete internal checklist to ensure all required sections are present, formatting follows sponsor rules, budgets are correct, and compliance items are addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translational framing where applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame projects with a bench-to-bedside/translational emphasis when appropriate (ITMAT framing, CHOP pediatric translation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If translational potential exists, explicitly state the pathway to clinical impact, including relevant Penn translational cores and partner institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize interdisciplinary bridging
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight interdisciplinary collaborations (e.g., Engineering + Medicine, Wharton + Medicine, SAS + Medicine).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how different disciplinary strengths combine to achieve the aims; articulate roles and integration plans to reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align proposal to funder-specific expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailor content to funder-specific themes: NIH conventions, NSF intellectual merit & broader impacts, DOE materials/energy focus, foundation strategic alignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For NIH: follow standard NIH conventions and institute priorities. For NSF: emphasize intellectual merit and broader impacts and consider industry partnerships. For DOE: highlight materials/energy relevance and national lab partnerships. For foundations: coordinate with Office of Foundation Relations and align strategically with foundation priorities; secure senior-leader letters where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative preliminary data
rubrics_metrics.description: Include quantitative preliminary data to support feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide data that demonstrate feasibility of key methods/assays and support proposed effect sizes/assumptions used in power/sample-size calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation framed as feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame innovation in a way that is both novel and feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid over-claiming novelty without feasible supporting methods; link innovative aspects to specific aims and preliminary data where possible.
